title: fix(plugin-security): explain credits read depth, not sharing, for a row only the depth admits
body:
Fixes #21726

Clause-②: no

The explain answer now produces `decidedBy: 'depth'`, a member the published `decidedBy` enum (`packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts`, about `:331`-`:341`) already declares. No access decision changes.

## What changed

All runtime changes are in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`, in the record-grained pass (`applyRecordAttribution`).

- **A row only read depth admits now explains as `decidedBy: 'depth'`.** The decision tree ranks `depth` with `sharing`: after a decisive bypass, after a share, and before `rls`. These are the two layers that widen a private baseline past its owner.
- **The `depth` layer carries a `record` block on record-grained requests.** It is `admitted` when the read depth admits the row, and it names the depth and, below `org`, the owner it reached. It is `excluded` when the owner is outside the depth. It is `not_evaluated` with a reason when the depth adds nothing (`own`, a non-private baseline, no record), when the depth cannot be separated (a share admits the row too, below `org`), or when the depth is not in play (an on-behalf-of read, a write).
- **The sharing layer reports `admitted` only when a share or rule matched.** For a row that only the depth admits, it is `not_evaluated`, and its detail says that no share grants the row and that read depth already admits it.
- **The sharing detail states a grant only when one exists.** "N share(s) attached; access is granted for this record." is kept for a share that names the caller. When the sharing filter admits a row with no such share, the detail names the part of the sharing service that let it through.
- `visible` comes from the same disjunction as before. `depthAdmitsRow` is the part of the old `sharingMatches === true` admission that the sharing layer no longer claims, so `sharingAdmitted || depthAdmitsRow` equals the old `sharingAdmitted`.

## How the depth admission is judged (measured, not re-derived)

The sharing read filter is one predicate with two grants: the owner-match, which read depth widens, OR-ed with the ids of the caller's own shares. Measured in plugin-sharing's `buildReadFilter`: at `org` depth it returns `null` and composes no owner-match at all. Below `org` it returns the owner-match over the depth's owners, OR-ed with `id IN (granted ids)` when the caller holds shares.

The engine does not parse that shape and does not call the filter a second time. It reads facts the pass already holds:

- the depth the `depth` layer published (`depthScope`);
- ownership;
- the share rows naming the caller (the grant disjunct's population);
- whether the filter matched.

Two cases are deliberately not credited to the depth. On an on-behalf-of read, `security-plugin.ts` hands the filter the delegated context with no depth stamped. Below `org`, a `null` filter means the sharing service imposes no owner-match on that object.

## Precedence when a share and the depth both admit

This case is not named on the card. `decidedBy`'s published contract decides it: "the layer whose `record.outcome` excluded it, or the last one to admit it" (`explain.zod.ts` about `:390`, and the `.describe` at `:342`). In pipeline order, depth comes before sharing, so a row a share admits keeps `decidedBy: 'sharing'`. That is also the answer before this change. The hand-written explain page (`content/docs/permissions/explain.mdx`) does not describe record verdict precedence, so no docs sentence became false.

## Tests

Tests were added or updated in `plugin-security`:

- `explain-engine.test.ts`, unit harness:
  - org depth and unit depth explain as `depth`, with a depth record block;
  - an owner outside the unit is excluded by both layers;
  - a criteria rule's share still explains as `sharing` with exactly "1 share(s) attached; access is granted for this record.";
  - share plus depth, at org and at unit;
  - the two guards (a null filter below org, and an on-behalf-of read).
- `explain-engine.test.ts`, enumeration: `decidedBy` is read from `ExplainDecisionSchema` in `@objectstack/spec/security`. The test fails by name for any member that no scenario produces and no ledger entry explains. Today `principal` and `fls` are ledgered with reasons, and every other member is produced by a scenario that drives its branch.
- `explain-read-verdict-inputs.test.ts`, real SecurityPlugin plus real SharingService:
  - decider cells: depth for org and unit readers; sharing for a manual share, a rule-sourced share row, and share plus depth; owd_baseline for the owner;
  - the depth record block;
  - the rule row's exact detail.

  The existing test that asserted the sharing layer `admitted` an org-depth row was re-judged and replaced: it pinned the behaviour this change removes. Each cell still asserts explain `visible` equals the find's outcome.
- `explain-dependency-fault.test.ts`: the "a null filter is an answer, not a fault" test now asserts `decidedBy: 'depth'`, with the filter published and judged. A faulted layer publishes neither.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (full package): 164 files, 3562 passed, 45 skipped, 0 failed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: exit 0. This includes `check:test-typecheck` over `tsconfig.test.json`, which compiles the test layer.

## Ablations (each red, then restored and proven: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty)

- A0, the whole file put back at the merge base (`ff29410e`): 15 failed out of 161 in the three explain files. Examples: `expected 'sharing' to be 'depth'`, and `expected '0 share(s) attached; access is grante…' to contain …`.
- A1, `depthAdmitsRow` forced false: 9 red. These are every depth decider cell and the `'depth' is produced` enumeration case.
- A2, the detail names a grant without a share: 2 red (the null-filter and on-behalf-of guards' detail assertions).
- A3, the on-behalf-of guard removed: 1 red.
- A4, the null-below-org guard removed: 1 red.
- A5, the `fls` ledger entry renamed: 1 red, with `decidedBy member 'fls' is produced by no branch and carries no ledger reason`.

The subject resolves from `src` (relative imports), so no dist rebuild was involved.

Each was re-run green after its stated build (`turbo` cache hits). The `--ran` reconciliation: 66 derived, 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

Lint was narrowed to the 4 touched `.ts` files. ① They are in the population of `eslint.config.mjs`'s `packages/**` objects (`--print-config` resolves for each). ② `--format json` reports 4 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. ③ The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.

## Acceptance notes

- **The write path has the same attribution shape and is left as it is.** For `update`/`delete`, the row verdict is the sharing service's per-record gate, which judges write depth, ownership and shares together. A write admitted by write depth still reads `decidedBy: 'sharing'`, with the gate detail naming ownership or a share. The new `depth` record block on a write says that this report does not separate the write depth. Carrier: none named.
- **The owner's row keeps its sharing-layer detail**, "Caller owns the record — visible without a share." It still decides as `owd_baseline`, which was already the case.
